version.changelog: Initial release: smoke/manual/check-telemetry helper, SID/telemetry invariant checks, CI gates

llm.summary: This skill is a coherent local CloudArc benchmark helper with disclosed resource costs and no evidence of hidden persistence, credential use, or data exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: The helper can run tests and benchmarks locally, and manual runs may consume hours and tens of GiB of temporary disk; this is disclosed and the manual path requires an explicit --yes flag.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is described as cloning into the skills directory or installing from the registry; no auto-running installer, remote payload retrieval, or dependency installation behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare explicit least-privilege tool metadata, but its runtime instructions constrain work to repository inspection, local tests/benchmarks, documentation updates, and explicitly prohibit cloud credentials, proprietary packages, commits, and editing Downloads source materials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoors, services, scheduled tasks, memory writes, credential harvesting, or cross-session persistence were found; CI workflow changes are purpose-aligned and user/repository-directed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is bounded-memory CloudArc benchmark, deduplication, telemetry, and CI gate validation; the instructions and helper script match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only for CloudArc repositories where you intend to run local tests and benchmarks. Review the manual benchmark settings before use because they can consume substantial time and disk, and avoid pointing --repo or --python at untrusted locations or executables.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Reading repository files and running local tests/benchmarks are expected for this benchmark workflow. The lack of explicit tool-scope metadata is a documentation gap, but artifact instructions include meaningful boundaries and do not support escalation to Review.
[AST4] expected: The subprocess use runs explicit Python unittest and benchmark commands with an argument list and no shell invocation. User-provided repo/python/options affect local benchmark execution, but this is purpose-aligned and disclosed.
